sections.title: Core business
sections.text: A fictional study for the demo. ASML Holding N.V. earns most of its revenue from euv systems and the lines around it; the segments and their shares are in the filings' revenue note.

sections.title: Growth
sections.text: Revenue grew about 15.1% a year from 2021 to 2025, and 15.6% over the trailing year. EUV systems is the fastest line.

sections.title: Profitability and returns on capital
sections.text: The operating margin is 34.6% and moved 2.7 points on the year; return on invested capital reads 99.0%.

sections.title: Segments and unit economics
sections.text: EUV systems grows faster than the company and carries a higher margin; the rest grows with the market.

sections.title: Competition and position
sections.text: Competitors are named in the filing; share has held over five years on the figures the company reports.

sections.title: Moats
sections.text: Scale and the network of customers on both sides are the advantages the study finds; each could erode if a rival matches the cost position.

sections.title: Valuation
sections.text: At 63x trailing earnings and 54x free cash flow, the price assumes about 18.4% a year of growth on the reverse DCF.

sections.title: Latest earnings
sections.text: The last four quarters beat the analysts' consensus on EPS; the guidance was kept at the last results.

sections.title: Capital allocation
sections.text: About 62% of free cash flow went back in buybacks and dividends.

sections.title: Owner's valuation
sections.text: On the base case the per-share value sits near the owner's base valuation; the bear case needs growth to halve.

sections.title: Strengths, weaknesses, opportunities, threats
sections.text: Strengths: EUV systems, margins. Weaknesses: concentration in one line. Opportunities: new markets. Threats: regulation and rivals.

sections.title: Key research question
sections.text: Does euv systems keep growing faster than the company for three more years? The study reads the figures as yes, with the guidance as the risk.

sections.title: Investment questions
sections.text: Whether the fastest line keeps its pace; whether the margin holds while the company invests; what the price assumes against that.

sections.title: Classification
sections.text: It tests as Transitional Holding on the filings' figures.

sections.title: Kill signals and sell discipline
sections.text: Engine growth below 15% is the kill signal on the record; it is not met on the latest figures.

sections.title: Conclusion
sections.text: A fictional conclusion: ASML stays a Transitional Holding; the price is above the owner's base value.

study.question: Does MA still test as a Compounding Machine after the third quarter, and is the price above the base value?

sections.title: Core business
sections.text: A fictional study for the demo. Mastercard Incorporated earns most of its revenue from value-added services and solutions and the lines around it; the segments and their shares are in the filings' revenue note.

sections.title: Growth
sections.text: Revenue grew about 14.5% a year from 2021 to 2025, and 16.0% over the trailing year. Value-added services and solutions is the fastest line.

sections.title: Profitability and returns on capital
sections.text: The operating margin is 58.3% and moved 2.6 points on the year; return on invested capital reads 98.0%.

sections.title: Segments and unit economics
sections.text: Value-added services and solutions grows faster than the company and carries a higher margin; the rest grows with the market.

sections.title: Competition and position
sections.text: Competitors are named in the filing; share has held over five years on the figures the company reports.

sections.title: Moats
sections.text: Scale and the network of customers on both sides are the advantages the study finds; each could erode if a rival matches the cost position.

sections.title: Valuation
sections.text: At 32x trailing earnings and 33x free cash flow, the price assumes about 12.1% a year of growth on the reverse DCF.

sections.title: Latest earnings
sections.text: The last four quarters beat the analysts' consensus on EPS; the guidance was kept at the last results.

sections.title: Capital allocation
sections.text: About 94% of free cash flow went back in buybacks and dividends.

sections.title: Owner's valuation
sections.text: On the base case the per-share value sits near the owner's base valuation; the bear case needs growth to halve.

sections.title: Strengths, weaknesses, opportunities, threats
sections.text: Strengths: Value-added services and solutions, margins. Weaknesses: concentration in one line. Opportunities: new markets. Threats: regulation and rivals.

sections.title: Key research question
sections.text: Does value-added services and solutions keep growing faster than the company for three more years? The study reads the figures as yes, with the guidance as the risk.

sections.title: Investment questions
sections.text: Whether the fastest line keeps its pace; whether the margin holds while the company invests; what the price assumes against that.

sections.title: Classification
sections.text: It tests as Transitional Holding on the filings' figures.

sections.title: Kill signals and sell discipline
sections.text: Revenue growth below 8% is the kill signal on the record; it is not met on the latest figures.

sections.title: Conclusion
sections.text: A fictional conclusion: MA stays a Transitional Holding; the price is above the owner's base value.
